public_rationale: The condition remains uncertain under the contextual reading of the broader AI boom. The geographic ambiguity is material and should prevent an automatic score. The conditional-forecast rule therefore requires not_adjudicable at this freeze. This does not mean the prediction is false or inherently uncheckable. It has no deadline, and no decisive event satisfying the stated rule has been established.
limitations: A narrower geographic interpretation could produce a different assessment.
Market optimism at one date cannot establish that a collapse never occurred later.
The search does not provide a complete event study through the cutoff.

statement.excerpt: There will be measurable damage to the stock market, but more importantly tens of thousands of people will lose their jobs and a depression will begin in the tech industry.

from_speaker: There will be measurable damage to the stock market
our_interpretation: The surrounding discussion makes this conditional on the AI bubble popping.
The plain reading is an observable stock-market loss attributable to a collapse of the AI investment boom discussed in the post.
The context points to the broader boom centered on major US technology companies. A regional collapse is relevant but does not automatically establish that antecedent.
Major US indexes and representative technology or AI stock baskets are reasonable measures. No minimum percentage loss is imposed.
No deadline or fixed period after the collapse is supplied.
criteria.support_condition: Independent evidence establishes the relevant AI-boom collapse, and market data with credible event analysis show an attributable loss in stock-market value.
criteria.contradiction_condition: The relevant collapse occurs and sufficiently complete market evidence establishes that it produced no measurable stock-market loss. Continued investment or the absence of a collapse cannot contradict the forecast.
